defects.description: The empty-data guard is `n < 0`, which can never be true for a length; empty input should be caught with `n == 0` (as the error message says), so `median([])` falls through and raises an IndexError instead.
paraphrases: `if n < 0` never fires; the guard should be `if n == 0` to reject empty data as the message states.
Empty input is not handled: a length is never negative, so `median([])` skips the check and crashes with IndexError.
The 'no median for empty data' guard is dead code because it tests `n < 0` instead of `n == 0`.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `if n == 0:`. Real (empty input crashes instead of a clean error), findable via the message/precondition, distinct.

defects.description: For odd-length data the function returns `data[n // 2 - 1]`, which is one position left of the true middle element (`data[n // 2]`).
paraphrases: The odd-case index is off by one: it should be `data[n // 2]`, not `data[n // 2 - 1]`.
`median([1, 3, 5])` returns 1 instead of the documented 3 because the middle index is shifted down by one.
The middle element for odd n is selected one slot too early.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `return data[n // 2]`. Real (wrong median for odd n), findable via the docstring example (3), distinct.

defects.description: For even-length data the two middle values are divided by 1 instead of 2, so the result is their sum rather than their average.
paraphrases: `(data[i - 1] + data[i]) / 1` should divide by 2; as written it returns the sum of the two middle values.
`median([1, 3, 5, 7])` returns 8 instead of the documented 4.0 because of the `/ 1`.
The even-case average is not halved: the divisor is 1, not 2.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `/ 2`. Real (even-length median doubled), findable via the docstring example (4.0), distinct from the odd-case defect.
